subject: Subprocessor impact snapshot and temporary residency safeguard — FinTechCorp renewal
messages:
From: Dana Lewis <dana.lewis@fintechcorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor roster + temporary onshore routing for renewal audit

Hi Karthik,

As we move toward the renewal signature next week, procurement asked me to request a consolidated roster of all third parties that process FinTechCorp data on Redwood's behalf (including sub-subprocessors and transit/caching partners). Specifically we need:

- Full roster with vendor roles and country of processing
- A simple dataflow map showing where customer PII traverses (ingest -> storage -> telemetry)
- Any planned subprocessor changes in the next 90 days

Separately, we have an upcoming audit window (Jan 20–24) and need a temporary onshore routing option so that European-origin data for our tenants can be routed through US-east instances for the duration of the audit. Can Redwood provide a temporary residency safeguard and confirm what contractual amendment (DPA addendum, SOW) would be required?

We appreciate a quick turnaround — can you share materials by EOD Thursday?

Thanks,
Dana
Dana Lewis
Senior IT Procurement
FinTechCorp

Attachment: none
From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Dana Lewis <dana.lewis@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + temporary onshore routing for renewal audit

Hi Dana — thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We can provide the roster and a compact dataflow map by your requested timeframe. To be explicit:

- We will deliver a consolidated subprocessor roster (including transit/cache partners and subprocessors used by telemetry/observability).
- We can draw a one‑page dataflow (ingest -> model serving -> logs/telemetry -> long‑term storage) highlighting processing jurisdictions.
- We will flag any planned changes within 90 days. Currently there are no scheduled decommissions that would affect your account.

On the temporary onshore routing: we can enable an onshore routing policy for the specified audit window, but it requires: either a DPA addendum (preferred) or a short SOW amendment that references the routing policy and confirms the audit dates and scope. We will need procurement to countersign.

Looping in Mina (Trust & Safety) to confirm what evidence we can provide for the roster and the exact control statements for the DPA addendum, and Marissa for procurement/DocuSign logistics.

Next steps I propose:
1) We deliver the roster + dataflow by Thu EOD (Jan 14).
2) Mina will propose language for a DPA addendum and a minimal checklist for the onshore routing (what logs, what retention).
3) Marissa will share a DocuSign cover sheet and PO guidance so we can get the amendment countersigned before Jan 20.

Sound good?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Lewis <dana.lewis@fintechcorp.com>, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + temporary onshore routing for renewal audit

Hi Dana — thanks for the note, and happy to help. A few clarifications and commitments from Redwood's side: 

1) Deliverables (target: Thu, Jan 14 EOD):
   - subprocessor_roster_20270113.pdf (complete list with role, country, encryption-at-rest status)
   - dataflow_map_20270113.xlsx (simple flow with processing jurisdiction columns)

2) Temporary onshore routing: we can enable an onshore routing safeguard scoped to your tenant(s) for Jan 20–24. Technical constraints:
   - Routing is implemented at the tenant routing layer and will direct eligible traffic to our US-east serving pool.
   - Telemetry/observability calls may still cross borders for aggregated metrics unless you opt into a limited retention profile (we can offer retention reduction for the audit period).

3) Contractual path: the minimal path is a DPA addendum that defines the routing window, affected tenant IDs, and retention adjustments. We will draft language that is intentionally narrow (dates + purpose). We can also do an SOW amendment if procurement prefers billing/PO alignment.

4) Evidence we can provide immediately: SOC 2 summary, KMS/HSM provider information, and a CSV extract of subprocessor endpoints. Full SOC2 report and some vendor contracts are provided under NDA; if FinTechCorp requires those, we'll coordinate an NDA + secure share.

I'll attach the roster/dataflow in the next note. Marissa — once Dana confirms procurement preference (DPA addendum vs SOW), we can route a DocuSign envelope and include the PO.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20270113.pdf; dataflow_map_20270113.xlsx

Team — appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed the roster and the map; those look good. Procurement prefers a short DPA addendum (one page) rather than an SOW so we can keep the commercial terms separate. Requested small edits:

- Please explicitly call out CDN/caching partners and their processing jurisdictions in the roster (we saw the entries but need the country column to be explicit).
- Confirm that the routing safeguard will apply to tenant IDs: fintechcorp-prod, fintechcorp-staging.

I've uploaded our PO and a signed procurement cover to speed countersignature: FinTechCorp_PO_789.pdf (attached). Our procurement contact is Aaron Flores (aaron.flores@fintechcorp.com) — he'll expect the DocuSign envelope.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/FinTechCorp/FT-2026-0023

Please proceed with the DPA addendum draft and route to Aaron + our procurement mailbox. Once signed we'll flip the routing on for Jan 20.

Thanks again — Dana
